design.scope: Minimal white creative-studio/video-editor UI patterns with Higgsfield as primary generation service

method.sources: Primary documentation and official product/help pages read directly where available; live pages can be dynamic or reader-incomplete.
method.uncertainty: Recommendations are design translations, not claims that FrameForge must copy any vendor UI. Exact product behavior should be rechecked against current provider APIs before shipping.

sources.title: Adobe Spectrum
observed_principles: Spectrum presents foundations, tokens, patterns, and components as one connected system rather than isolated widgets.
The system emphasizes components in context and consistent behavior across platforms.
sources.frameforge_translation: Define a small neutral token layer first, then use the same panel, field, badge, button, disclosure, and dialog rules in Studio, Workflow, History, and Settings.

sources.title: React Aria Dialog
observed_principles: Dialogs expose a focused interaction surface and associate title/description semantics.
Focus management and keyboard behavior are treated as part of the component contract, not optional styling.
sources.frameforge_translation: Keep existing native dialog flow, ensure every title is labelled, put focus on the safe action for destructive/paid confirmations, preserve focus on close, and make Escape/cancel reliable.

sources.title: React Aria Disclosure
observed_principles: Disclosure lets users reveal secondary content without making the initial surface dense.
The trigger and expanded state must remain understandable to keyboard and assistive technology users.
sources.frameforge_translation: In generation inspector, show connection state, model, target scene, prompt, and primary action first; place model parameters, advanced coordinates, and recovery details behind labelled details/disclosure sections.
sources.tradeoff: Hidden options reduce cognitive load but can reduce discoverability; use explicit labels such as '고급 모델 설정' and preserve expanded state during edits.

sources.title: React Spectrum Form
observed_principles: Forms pair labels, validation, and submission affordances as one pattern.
Required/invalid states should be communicated in the field context, not only through color.
sources.frameforge_translation: Keep labels visible, use hint text for model parameters, expose validation beside the field, and avoid relying on pale borders or color-only status badges.

sources.title: GOV.UK Details component
observed_principles: Details makes a page easier to scan by revealing additional information only when needed.
The component is intentionally simple and works with native disclosure semantics.
sources.frameforge_translation: Use native details/summary for advanced workflow settings, provider diagnostics, and long explanatory copy; do not hide safety-critical cost, status, or error information.
sources.tradeoff: Progressive disclosure is unsuitable for side-by-side comparisons or information users must always see; keep current status and paid-action warnings visible.

sources.title: GOV.UK Error summary
observed_principles: Validation errors should be summarized and linked to the relevant fields so users can recover quickly.
Error copy should explain what is wrong and how to fix it.
sources.frameforge_translation: For generation model/parameter failures, show a compact alert summary above the inspector and field-level messages with recovery guidance; retain requestId/providerRequestId for support and recovery instead of hiding them in a toast.

sources.title: GOV.UK Task list
observed_principles: Complex multi-step work benefits from explicit task states such as not started, in progress, and complete.
The task list is a progress/navigation aid, not a replacement for simplifying a process.
sources.frameforge_translation: Represent Workflow node states with text labels and status hierarchy; do not make users infer queued/running/completed/failed from color or icons alone.

sources.title: GOV.UK Validation pattern
observed_principles: Validation should tell users what is wrong and how to correct it, close to the affected answer.
A clear page-level error summary supports scanning while field messages support correction.
sources.frameforge_translation: Keep provider status distinction explicit: 연결 확인 필요, 설정됨·검증 필요, 연결됨; when a generation call fails, name the next safe action (refresh, recover known request, or inspect history) rather than suggesting blind retry.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group Progressive Disclosure
observed_principles: Advanced or rarely used features can move to secondary surfaces so the initial interface stays learnable.
Progressive disclosure is not appropriate where users need side-by-side comparison or continuously visible safety-critical information.
sources.frameforge_translation: Keep the editor's first view calm: primary scene controls and one obvious next action; disclose advanced generation parameters, workflow coordinates, and diagnostics only on demand.
sources.tradeoff: Do not collapse history comparisons, paid cost details, provider request identity, or unsaved-change warnings; these are needed for safe decisions and recovery.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Contrast (Minimum)
observed_principles: Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text requires at least 3:1.
Faint gray helper text on a white canvas is not acceptable simply because it looks minimal.
sources.frameforge_translation: Use dark neutral body text (#101828 or similar), readable secondary text (#475467 or darker), and verify every intended text/color pair with a contrast checker.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Target Size Minimum
observed_principles: Pointer targets should be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless an exception applies.
Spacing can prevent small adjacent controls from accidentally colliding.
sources.frameforge_translation: Set compact buttons/icon buttons to at least 24px hit areas, preferably 32px for the white toolbar; add spacing between nav, history version, close, and disclosure controls.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Status Messages
observed_principles: Important status changes that do not move focus must be programmatically determinable so assistive technologies can announce them.
A toast alone is insufficient when the underlying status is important to the workflow.
sources.frameforge_translation: Keep an aria-live region for save/generation state, but also render durable status text in the generation result panel and workflow node; do not rely on color or transient toasts.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Error Prevention
observed_principles: Important submissions that modify/delete data or cause financial commitments need reversibility, checking, or confirmation.
The user should be able to confirm, correct, or reverse consequential submissions.
sources.frameforge_translation: Preserve FrameForge's explicit Higgsfield consent dialog, show model/cost context before send, persist submission intent before spending, recover only known provider IDs, and require an explicit Apply action for completed output.

sources.title: Adobe Premiere workspace documentation
observed_principles: Premiere organizes complex post-production work into named workspaces and dockable panels instead of putting every control into one screen.
Workspaces make role-specific tasks discoverable while preserving a stable editing context.
sources.frameforge_translation: Keep FrameForge's Studio, Workflow, History, and Settings as clear top-level destinations, but use one consistent white shell and local panel hierarchy rather than decorative dashboard cards.
sources.tradeoff: Too many top-level destinations can dilute focus; keep generation and history near the workflow where users need them, while preserving existing routes for compatibility.
sources.confidence: medium (page is long and reader extraction is partial)

sources.title: Higgsfield AI product surface
observed_principles: Higgsfield positions itself as a creative suite for image, video, voice, editing/upscale, and automated workflows across web and mobile.
The product surface is model/content oriented, so FrameForge should keep provider-specific complexity behind a stable generation inspector.
sources.frameforge_translation: Use Higgsfield as the named provider in connection/status and generation result surfaces, while keeping the editor's task language model-agnostic enough to preserve history and provider-state distinctions.
sources.uncertainty: The public homepage is dynamic and does not establish exact API credit or billing semantics; treat provider pricing as a confirmation-time fact from the authenticated adapter, not a hardcoded UI claim.

sources.title: Higgsfield pricing
observed_principles: Pricing is presented as a separate product surface and may vary by plan/model.
A public pricing page alone does not provide a reliable per-request estimate for every model/parameter combination.
sources.frameforge_translation: Do not hardcode a generic cost label. Show the provider estimate returned by /api/generation/status or estimate flow when available, otherwise state that cost verification is required before submission.
sources.uncertainty: Reader extraction returned page metadata but not detailed plan values, likely due dynamic rendering/auth context.

design_brief.direction: Calm white production tool: content first, neutral surfaces, compact but readable controls, one primary action per panel, visible workflow state, no marketing hero treatment.

tokens.type: 13px UI base, 14-16px body, 28-32px page heading; use weight/spacing before oversized type

layout: Use a white content canvas with a low-contrast page background and 1px panel boundaries; avoid heavy shadows.
Keep sidebar/nav stable, but make the active route obvious through text, background tint, and aria-current rather than icon-only highlighting.
Use a single-column field stack in inspectors; reserve two-column layouts for truly related short fields on wide screens and reflow them on narrow screens.
Keep current generation status, request identity, cost/confirmation state, and unsaved-change warnings visible; disclose advanced parameters and diagnostics.
accessibility: Text contrast >=4.5:1; large text >=3:1; validate intended border/focus treatment for non-text contrast.
At least 24x24 CSS px targets; 32px preferred for toolbar/icon controls.
Preserve visible focus rings (2px or stronger), keyboard order, and native dialog Escape/cancel behavior.
Use aria-live for asynchronous save/generation updates plus durable status text in the relevant panel.
Error summaries should link to fields and tell the user the next corrective/recovery action; never expose provider secrets.

priority_fixes.change: Replace dark green/lime palette with white/neutral tokens above; preserve hierarchy using border, spacing, and restrained blue primary; ensure text and focus contrast.
priority_fixes.why: The current root declares color-scheme:dark and dark surfaces, contrary to requested white calm tool direction and W3C contrast guidance.

priority_fixes.change: Set theme-color to the white/neutral shell value (for example #f7f8fa) so browser chrome does not contradict the UI.
priority_fixes.why: The current value is #121512 while the redesign is white.

priority_fixes.change: Use neutral panel hierarchy, low-contrast dividers, and clear primary/secondary ordering; retain existing responsive breakpoints and disclosure behavior.
priority_fixes.why: Workflow and history are dense product surfaces where progressive disclosure and explicit states matter more than decorative color.

priority_fixes.symbols: generationControlsHtml(node), generationParameterHtml(field, params), dialogsHtml(), generationJobHtml(id), nodeResultsHtml(node)
priority_fixes.change: Keep connection badge and status text visible; group secondary model parameters in labelled details; make paid confirmation show exact model and provider estimate when available; keep recover/apply semantics and request IDs visible in result/recovery panel.
priority_fixes.why: WCAG error prevention/status messages plus existing FrameForge safety contract require cost confirmation, known-request recovery, and explicit Apply.

priority_fixes.symbols: render(), heading(), studioView(), historyView(), toast/status regions
priority_fixes.change: Clarify one primary page action, reduce heading/action competition, use durable inline status beside transient toast, and style history as an explicit version list/comparison rather than decorative cards.
priority_fixes.why: Premiere-style named workspaces and GOV.UK task/status patterns support stable navigation and visible state for complex production work.

priority_fixes.change: Keep skip link and aria-current, verify all icon-only buttons have labels, and ensure async generation/save messages are announced without moving focus.
priority_fixes.why: WCAG target size/status message guidance; minimal visual design must not remove semantic cues.

non_goals: Do not redesign provider/server safety semantics.
Do not remove episode/workflow history, optimistic concurrency, requestId recovery, or explicit generation Apply.
Do not claim Higgsfield credits/prices from public marketing pages when the authenticated provider estimate is unavailable.
Do not add hero cards, marketing gradients, or a second component framework.

higgsfield.title: FrameForge Studio Higgsfield generation UX/API research

scope.boundary: Research only. No provider credentials, paid generation, or repository edits were performed.

sources.title: Higgsfield API documentation index
evidence: The selected model's model-specific documentation is authoritative for endpoint and schema; /docs/openapi.json is supplementary.
The API is server-side and model availability is account-dependent.

sources.title: Authentication
evidence: Use Authorization: Key YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET; legacy hf-api-key/hf-secret headers remain accepted.
Credentials must remain server-side; browser/mobile API calls are explicitly prohibited.
Authentication identifies the account, but a model can still be unavailable and return 404, 423, or 503.

sources.title: How the API works
evidence: Generation is asynchronous: submit JSON, store request_id, poll status_url or receive a webhook, then download output.
Base URL is https://api.higgsfield.ai.

sources.title: Requests and lifecycle
evidence: Documented states are queued, in_progress, completed, failed, nsfw, and canceled.
The initial receipt contains request_id, status_url, and cancel_url; clients should use returned URLs rather than reconstructing them.
Completed output shape varies by media type (images[], video.url, audio.url, and some additional artifacts).

sources.title: Idempotent requests
evidence: Generation POSTs accept Idempotency-Key (1-255 visible ASCII characters, UUID recommended).
On ambiguous timeout/network/5xx, repeat the same endpoint/body/webhook with the same key; the original request_id is returned without another charge.
Reusing a key with changed endpoint/body/webhook returns 422 and must not trigger automatic new-key generation.
Status polling, uploads, estimates, and webhook deliveries use their existing retry behavior.

sources.title: Polling
evidence: Start around two seconds, increase gradually up to ten seconds, and add jitter.
Stop on completed, failed, nsfw, or canceled.
Retry GET status after network failures/5xx with backoff; stop on 401 or 404.
Use webhooks for long-running production workloads while retaining polling as recovery.

sources.title: Errors and retries
evidence: 400 includes malformed/rejected input or concurrency reached; 401 credentials; 403 insufficient credits; 404 account/model/request not found; 422 validation or idempotency mismatch; 423 temporarily blocked; 500/503 later retry cases.
Accepted jobs may later end failed or nsfw; these are not charged and reserved credits are refunded.
Every response includes X-Correlation-ID; record it with request_id for support.

sources.title: Billing, estimation, and retention
evidence: POST /estimate/{model} with the exact generation parameters returns authoritative account-specific credits and usd values.
Successful generation requests consume credits; output URLs are available for at least seven days and should be copied to owned storage for long-term retention.
Canceled queued requests are refunded; failed/nsfw requests are not charged.

sources.title: Official client libraries
evidence: Official Python and TypeScript SDKs are server-side only and handle auth, submission, polling, cancellation, uploads, and retries.
Explicit lifecycle APIs (submit/status/result/cancel) are recommended for workers; webhooks plus polling recovery are recommended for production event-driven integration.

sources.title: Higgsfield CLI README
evidence: CLI is a separate terminal product with auth login/logout/token, model list/get, generate create, wait, cost, and jobs commands.
The CLI documents short-lived auth sessions, HIGGSFIELD_TOKEN as a non-interactive alternative, and dynamic model discovery via higgsfield model list.
CLI install/release is independent from the REST API credentials and from FrameForge's MCP bridge.

sources.title: CLI model catalog
evidence: Generated catalog lists current CLI job_set_type schemas, required flags, defaults, enum values, and media-reference constraints.
Local media flags can accept UUIDs or paths that the CLI uploads; this is distinct from FrameForge's REST asset URL allowlist.

sources.title: Higgsfield Node/TypeScript SDK
evidence: The v2 client exposes server-side credentials, automatic polling/retries, and explicit lifecycle methods; its documented defaults include a two-minute timeout, maxRetries 3, retry backoff, and two-second poll interval.
SDK usage is a possible future dependency, but the current no-dependency FrameForge architecture can preserve its own bounded adapter instead.

restApi.credential: HF_API_KEY or HF_CREDENTIALS, sent as Authorization: Key <id>:<secret>
restApi.currentStatus: Configured means a non-empty credential is present; capability reports configured/available without making a verification request.
restApi.importantGap: createHiggsfieldApi.call does not send Idempotency-Key or retain X-Correlation-ID/status_url/cancel_url from the receipt.

cli.credential: Higgsfield CLI login session or HIGGSFIELD_TOKEN on the host; FrameForge receives only AGENT_BRIDGE_TOKEN to call the local bridge.
cli.currentStatus: Dynamic catalog/schema and create/status are delegated to the authenticated host process; transport is recorded as cli.
cli.importantGap: CLI cost/estimate and provider correlation headers are not represented in the FrameForge provider contract.

projectOwnedMcp.credential: FRAMEFORGE_TOKEN or LOGIN_TOKEN authenticates to FrameForge /api/login; it is not an official Higgsfield MCP credential.
projectOwnedMcp.safety: The bridge explicitly labels itself project-owned, never replays POSTs after a 401/network ambiguity, and separates recover from create/apply.

modelDiscovery.api: Hardcoded and manually verified Seedance 2.5 mapping in server/higgsfield.mjs:13-24; unknown API models fail with INVALID_INPUT.
modelDiscovery.cli: Dynamic /generation/models and /generation/models?model=... through the host bridge (server/generation-provider.mjs:28-35).
modelDiscovery.ui: public/workflow.js:278-290 loads status and catalog concurrently, then fetches the selected schema; it preserves a saved model even when the current catalog no longer contains it.

currentFrameForgeCapabilities.schemaValidation: GenerationQueue.start validates model schema and parameters before persisting a billable job or spending (server/generations.mjs:96-117). It rejects prompt overrides and bounds JSON size.
currentFrameForgeCapabilities.estimate: CLI bridge exposes estimate, but the API adapter deliberately throws UNSUPPORTED at server/higgsfield.mjs:114-116. UI currently has no authoritative credits/USD preflight in generationControlsHtml.
currentFrameForgeCapabilities.asyncLifecycle: GenerationQueue persists intent, submits once, stores providerRequestId, polls, imports owned media, and distinguishes queued/submitting/pending/in_progress/downloading/completed/failed/nsfw/canceled/polling_failed/import_failed/manual_recovery (server/generations.mjs:32-183).
currentFrameForgeCapabilities.idempotency: FrameForge requestId deduplicates locally and rejects changed payloads (server/generations.mjs:71-94; tests/generations.test.mjs:69-83), but provider REST idempotency is not sent. An ambiguous provider submission becomes submission_unknown rather than an automatic replay.
currentFrameForgeCapabilities.outputApply: Completed provider URLs are downloaded through a strict Higgsfield host allowlist, hashed/probed, stored as generated uploads with provenance, and applied only by an explicit versioned action (server/generations.mjs:186-221, 271-277). UI exposes refresh/recover/apply separately (public/workflow.js:292-307).
currentFrameForgeCapabilities.concurrencyAndRecovery: Queue maxActive defaults to four; polling has a max duration and failure count; restart resumes only known provider IDs and refuses changed transports (server/generations.mjs:49-69, 134-183).
currentFrameForgeCapabilities.mediaBoundary: Scene generation accepts image/video only; audio and other API artifacts are not attachable even though Higgsfield REST lifecycle docs include audio and additional artifacts.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Bind FrameForge requestId to Higgsfield REST Idempotency-Key
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Create/persist a provider idempotency key before the first REST POST (for example a stable FrameForge-scoped key derived from requestId), send it unchanged on ambiguous retry, and persist the exact model endpoint/body fingerprint. On replay, accept the original request_id and continue status polling; never mint a new key automatically for a changed body.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: Local requestId prevents duplicate FrameForge jobs but currently cannot make a lost REST submission safe at the vendor boundary. Official Higgsfield guidance requires Idempotency-Key for ambiguous timeout/network/5xx recovery.
prioritizedRecommendations.safetyInvariant: One intended generation has one provider idempotency key; unknown submission is recoverable by same-key replay or history inspection, never a fresh billable request.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Make estimation authoritative before consent
files: public/workflow.js:264-291 and generation run confirmation handler
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Implement POST /estimate/{model} in the API adapter using the same validated model/body as create; normalize credits/usd plus account/model availability. Surface the estimate in the generation inspector and run-confirm dialog, and require explicit consent after showing the current estimate. Keep CLI estimate as a separate transport capability; show unavailable rather than guessing.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: Official billing docs define estimate as account-specific and authoritative. The current API adapter always returns UNSUPPORTED, so the UI cannot give a cost preview for the primary REST path.
prioritizedRecommendations.safetyInvariant: No provider create call occurs before user consent that names model, parameters, and current estimate or explicitly states estimate unavailable.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Preserve provider receipt metadata and correlation evidence
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Persist status_url, cancel_url when returned, X-Correlation-ID, provider error detail/status, and the account transport. Poll returned status_url rather than constructing it where possible; retain request_id as the stable identity.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: Official requests docs say returned URLs are the source of truth and errors docs require X-Correlation-ID with request_id for support. Current code reconstructs requests/{id}/status and drops response headers/details.
prioritizedRecommendations.safetyInvariant: Recovery/support can identify the exact account, transport, request_id, status URL, and correlation ID without exposing credentials.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Adopt bounded backoff and jitter for REST polling
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Replace the fixed 2500 ms queue cadence for provider polling with provider-aware backoff (start ~2 s, cap ~10 s, bounded random jitter), while retaining maxPollFailures/maxPollDurationMs and explicit recover. Do not retry 401/404 or terminal states.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: This follows official polling guidance and reduces load/concurrency pressure. Existing fixed polling is safe but less efficient and can synchronize many jobs.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Treat catalog and account access as separate facts
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Keep API model mappings explicitly verified and label them as documented/verified mapping, not a complete live catalog. Keep CLI dynamic catalog separate. Capability should distinguish credential configured, account authenticated, model accessible, and provider operational; 404/423/503 must not be flattened into generic connected.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: Higgsfield documentation says the model catalog is account-dependent and model-specific docs are authoritative. The existing UI already has a useful configured/verified distinction; preserve and extend it.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Retain explicit output apply and owned-storage retention
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Keep the current download/hash/probe/provenance/apply split. Consider a clear retention warning that provider output URLs may disappear after at least seven days; never auto-apply generated output. Continue preserving failed/nsfw/canceled terminal states and imported originals.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: The current architecture already matches the safest contract and official retention semantics. This is a UX/documentation reinforcement, not a migration.

prioritizedRecommendations.title: Keep CLI and MCP as optional operator paths, not the primary browser transport
prioritizedRecommendations.change: Make REST API the primary provider when configured; expose CLI as an authenticated host-bridge fallback and MCP as a project-owned agent interface over FrameForge. Do not put Higgsfield secrets in browser, workflow JSON, MCP arguments, logs, or URLs.
prioritizedRecommendations.why: The three auth surfaces are intentionally distinct: REST server credentials, host CLI session/token, and FrameForge session token for MCP. Conflating them would expand blast radius and violate vendor guidance.

safetyInvariantsToPreserve: Credentials remain server/host-side; browser and project-owned MCP never receive Higgsfield key material.
Persist submission intent before any provider create call.
Local requestId is immutable for one generation intent and rejects changed payloads.
Ambiguous submission never auto-submits a new generation; recovery polls/replays only the same known provider identity or same provider idempotency key.
Provider transport is persisted and changed transports require manual recovery instead of silent cross-transport polling.
Schema/parameter validation and episode version checks complete before billable submission.
Provider statuses remain distinct, including nsfw and canceled/cancelled, and terminal failures are not mislabeled as success.
Generated media is downloaded only from trusted Higgsfield asset hosts, bounded, hashed, MIME/stream-probed, and stored with sanitized provenance.
Generation output is never applied automatically; apply requires explicit user action and the exact current episode version/scene.
Stale apply preserves the paid output and allows explicit reconciliation to the surviving scene; no output is discarded to hide concurrency conflicts.
No live paid generation, credential use, or publication is part of research or verification.
recommendedImplementationOrder: 1. Add provider idempotency key and receipt/correlation persistence without changing UI behavior.
2. Add REST estimate and estimate-unavailable UI state, then gate run confirmation on explicit consent.
3. Extend status handling to preserve returned status_url/cancel_url and account/model access distinctions.
4. Tune polling backoff/jitter and keep existing bounded recovery semantics.
5. Add retention/cost/recovery copy and regression tests for same-key replay, parameter mismatch, estimate gating, and metadata persistence.
higgsfield.bottomLine: FrameForge already has the correct high-level safety shape for a Higgsfield-primary standalone studio: server-side credentials, schema discovery before spend, persisted intent, provider-ID recovery, bounded media import, optimistic versioning, and explicit apply. The highest-risk missing contract is vendor-level REST idempotency and receipt metadata; the highest UX gap is authoritative account-specific estimation before the existing generation-consent gate.

scope.mode: read-only; no files in the repository edited; no formatter/linter/project-wide test suite run

boot.flow: HTML shell loads styles.css, workflow.css, and ES module app.js; app.js constructs the workflow editor and then renders the selected view into #app. #modal and hidden media/audio file inputs are global shared surfaces.

appShell.flow: api() is the single same-origin fetch wrapper with credentials, JSON error conversion, and 401 login recovery. refresh() hydrates /api/state. handleAction() owns view/channel/episode navigation, save-on-navigation, rendering, narration, history and integration actions.

workflowEditor.flow: createWorkflowEditor() keeps an in-memory workflow draft, saved snapshot, revision, dirty state, 40-step draft undo/redo, history versions, selected node, run polling and generation job state. shell()/paint() render the canvas and inspector. selectNode() drives one inspector surface; generationControlsHtml()/generationJobHtml() are the only generation settings/recovery UI.

serverContracts.security: Same-origin and loopback-host restrictions are checked before API access; API routes require authentication; CSP is self-only with media blob/data allowances.

provider.primaryUIPath: Higgsfield generation node in public/workflow.js; model catalog/schema and status are loaded from /api/generation/status and /api/generation/models.
provider.important: Higgsfield transport can be Developer API or authenticated official CLI/bridge. The UI must preserve configured vs authenticated vs available distinctions and must not infer paid readiness from a configured credential alone.

navigation_and_generation_flow: Studio render() presents scene cards, preview, narration, jobs and assistant; app state has one current episode and sceneIndex.
Selecting Workflow calls workflowEditor.load(); workflow shell exposes saved workflow, target episode, save/run buttons, canvas and inspector.
Selecting a node calls selectNode(); selecting generate additionally triggers loadGeneration(), which concurrently fetches provider capability and model catalog/schema.

Running a workflow with a generate node opens a confirmation dialog; only confirm-generation-run sends allowGeneration:true to POST /api/workflows/:id/run. A normal run cannot spend generation credits.

Run results are shown in inspector results; generation jobs poll known IDs, can recover polling/import failures, and completed outputs require explicit apply to a scene. Applying is versioned and does not submit a new generation.
History and restore are separate views/controls. Navigation auto-saves dirty episode/workflow drafts, while restore and reload are blocked when dirty to protect local edits.

findings.title: Current visual language is dark, dense and tokenless at component level
evidence: public/index.html:6-9 sets dark #121512 theme-color and two global stylesheets
public/styles.css:1-3 defines --bg:#111411, --surface:#191d19, --raised:#222722, --text:#edf1e8 and --lime/#coral accents
public/workflow.css:1-50 uses the same dark variables and dense canvas/inspector rules
findings.impact: A white-background redesign can be low-risk if it changes the shared tokens and semantic surface rules first; duplicated selector-level colors would create inconsistent editor/history/generation states.
findings.recommendation: Keep DOM and data attributes stable. Replace the root tokens and theme-color, then add explicit semantic tokens for canvas, panel, border, muted text, focus, success, warning and destructive states. Preserve status classes (.queued/.running/.completed/.failed/.awaiting_review), data-testid hooks and responsive media queries.

findings.title: Do not build a second Higgsfield form in Studio
evidence: public/workflow.js:220-238 inspectorHtml() routes settings/results/history
public/workflow.js:264-290 generationControlsHtml() loads status/catalog/schema and renders model/parameter controls
public/workflow.js:292-307 generationJobHtml()/loadGenerationJob() own request status, recovery and apply affordances
findings.impact: A separate CTA panel would duplicate schema fields and diverge from request recovery/apply safeguards.
findings.recommendation: Route the Studio CTA into the existing workflow inspector. Add a narrow public workflowEditor.openGeneration() seam, not a direct generation API call. Reuse inspectorHtml(), generationControlsHtml() and generationJobHtml() unchanged.

findings.title: A Higgsfield CTA needs a draft-only workflow entry seam
evidence: public/app.js:40-53 constructs workflowEditor; public/app.js:415 switches view and calls workflowEditor.load()
public/workflow.js:127-140 load() returns no workflow when /api/workflows is empty
public/workflow.js:510-513 new/add-node create in-memory drafts and mark them dirty
public/workflow.js:622-623 public API currently exposes load,mount,save,hasChanges,html only
findings.impact: Without a seam, a Studio CTA must either duplicate node creation or call internal DOM actions; both are fragile. Auto-saving would create an unintended workflow snapshot before the user reviews it.
findings.recommendation: Expose openGeneration() beside load/mount/save. It should await load() without force; if no workflow exists, create the same initialGraph() draft and add one generate node through a shared helper. If a workflow exists, select its existing generate node or add one to the in-memory draft. Set inspectorTab='settings', call changed()/paint(), and stop. The caller then sets view='workflow' and render(). Do not call save(), run, /api/episodes/:id/generations, or allowGeneration.

findings.title: Generated node is optional and currently absent from initialGraph
evidence: public/workflow.js:24-27 initialGraph() excludes generate
public/workflow.js:67-69 validates generation only when present
public/workflow.js:513 creates generate with model seedance_2_5, empty prompt/params and sceneIndex 0
scripts/usability-browser-smoke.py:123-137 explicitly adds generate via UI before testing it
findings.impact: The CTA must add the optional node without silently changing the saved workflow or bypassing graph validation. New draft must remain visibly unsaved until user chooses Save.
findings.recommendation: Factor the node literal from add-node into createNode(type, position). For CTA insertion, connect storyboard -> generate -> render and remove the direct storyboard -> render edge only if the product wants generation as the selected path; otherwise preserve the existing direct edge and let validation retain optional-branch semantics. Prefer preserving existing edges for an existing workflow.

findings.title: Status copy must preserve three provider states

preserved_invariants: Episode and workflow identities, versions and immutable history snapshots remain stable; restore appends a new version with a restore reason rather than rewriting old history.
All episode/workflow writes carry expectedVersion semantics; stale edits return 409 and must not overwrite newer state.
Dirty drafts are protected across navigation and restore/reload; save conflicts preserve local edits and require a deliberate retry.
Workflow validation preserves required script/storyboard/render/review counts, acyclic graph, connected graph and required ordering; generate remains optional unless explicitly inserted.
No generation is submitted by ordinary workflow run; only explicit user confirmation sends allowGeneration:true.
Generation intent is persisted before provider spend; requestId is portable/idempotent; changed payloads reject; ambiguous provider submissions never auto-retry.
After restart/recovery, only a known provider request ID on the original transport is polled; submission_unknown/manual_recovery cannot silently resubmit.
Provider status distinctions remain truthful: configured, authenticated and available are separate facts; unavailable/error details stay visible without leaking credentials.
Provider outputs are imported into local storage with verified identity/hash and safe host/redirect constraints; provider CDN URLs are not treated as permanent app assets.
Generation results are never auto-applied: completed output requires explicit apply with expectedVersion and sceneId; stale apply retains the paid output for reconciliation.
Completed workflow runs remain awaiting_review until human review; no automatic approval or channel publication is introduced.
Same-origin/auth/CSP protections and safe URL/media rendering remain intact.
